title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell–derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection.
analysis.methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to analyze duodenal biopsies and enteroids from individuals with chronic norovirus infection.
analysis.main_results: Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11, respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of immunodeficient individuals, which may not fully represent the natural course of norovirus infection in the general population.

analysis.summary_en: This study used single-cell RNA sequencing to investigate the pathogenesis of norovirus in the duodenum. It found that norovirus primarily infects enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with late enterocytes producing higher viral yields than M2 macrophages. The infection leads to dysregulation of immune responses, potentially driving pathogenesis.

title: Integrated molecular and epidemiological assessment of pediatric viral gastroenteritis using qRT-PCR versus rapid immunochromatographic diagnostics

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viral gastroenteritis represents a major cause of pediatric morbidity, being one of the leading acute conditions requiring emergency care or hospitalization. Enteric viruses such as rotavirus, norovirus, adenovirus, astrovirus, and sapovirus are frequently implicated, with prevalence varying by age and season.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The objective of this study was to assess the distribution of viral agents in children and to compare the performance of two diagnostic methods: immunochromatographic (ICT) and quantitative real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). In a retrospective study, a total of 164 children hospitalized with acute gastroenteritis between February 2023 and March 2025 were investigated using qRT-PCR and ICT methods.
analysis.methods: rotavirus was the predominant pathogen (66 cases by qRT-PCR; 32 by ICT), followed by norovirus (41 cases vs. 11), while viral co-infections accounted for 11% of cases. Although rapid ICT tests may serve as an initial diagnostic tool in settings with limited access to molecular testing, qRT-PCR provides more reliable pathogen detection and may improve the accuracy of etiological diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: The positivity rate for rotavirus, norovirus and adenovirus was 58.5% by qRT-PCR compared to 25.0% by ICT, with slightly higher rates in urban areas (62/103) and in females (54/73). The most affected age group was 1-3 years, with increased incidence during warm seasons.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings demonstrated a higher diagnostic performance of qRT-PCR compared with ICT, particularly for the detection of norovirus and rotavirus. These findings highlight the importance of rapid and accurate etiological diagnosis for appropriate management, prevention of complications, and reduction of unnecessary antibiotic use.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights into the diagnostic accuracy of qRT-PCR for norovirus and rotavirus in pediatric gastroenteritis, which can inform improved surveillance and diagnostic strategies in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The clinical impact of molecular testing on treatment decisions, antibiotic prescriptions, hospitalization duration, and patient outcomes was not assessed in this study. The evidence is moderate as the study is retrospective and does not evaluate clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of qRT-PCR versus rapid immunochromatographic tests (ICT) for viral gastroenteritis in children. Conducted in a retrospective setting, it analyzed 164 hospitalized children between February 2023 and March 2025. qRT-PCR showed higher positivity rates for norovirus and rotavirus compared to ICT, with rotavirus being the most prevalent pathogen. The study highlights the importance of accurate diagnosis for managing pediatric gastroenteritis and reducing unnecessary antibiotic use. However, it does not assess the clinical impact of molecular testing on treatment decisions or patient outcomes. The evidence is moderate due to the retrospective design and lack of outcome evaluation.

title: Impact to Healthcare-Associated Viral Gastroenteritis Infection Rate Using Different Visitation Models in a Pediatric Hospital.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pediatric healthcare-associated viral gastroenteritis infections (HA-VGI) contribute to morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and outbreaks. Visitor-related transmission is a recognized risk factor; associations between visitation models and HA-VGI incidence remain understudied.
analysis.study_design_and_population: HA-VGI rates were compared across four visitation models: (Period 1) seasonal visitation, visitors <13 years restricted December 1-April 30; (Period 2) two legally authorized representatives (LAR) permitted, mandatory masking; (Period 3) masking with an LAR-approved 10-person visitor list, including siblings; (Period 4) identical visitation model without masking (December 2017-June 2025).
analysis.methods: HA-VGI was defined as gastroenteritis on or after hospital day 3. Changepoint analysis, interrupted time series modeling, nonparametric comparisons, and multivariable linear regression assessed differences across periods. Regression models adjusted for community GI viral activity and calendar month. Rates were compared by unit and pathogen.
analysis.main_results: Median HA-VGI rates declined significantly during Period 2 compared with Period 1 (0.93 vs. 5.14 per 10,000 patient days; p<0.001). Although rates increased in Period 3, they remained below Period 1. Period 4 did not significantly differ from Period 1. Community GI viral activity was independently associated with HA-VGI rates (β=5.94; p=0.002). ICU rates were lower than non-ICU rates; norovirus predominated.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Adjusted regression demonstrated lower rates during Periods 2 and 3 than during Period 1 (β=-3.01 and -3.07, respectively; both p<0.001). Mandatory masking was associated with lower HA-VGI rates independent of community viral activity and seasonality and may provide protection during increased GI viral circulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that mandatory masking during visitation may reduce HA-VGI rates, offering a potential public health strategy to mitigate viral transmission in pediatric hospitals. These results may inform hospital policies on visitor restrictions and infection control measures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on observational data and does not establish causality. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of randomized control trials and potential confounding factors not fully accounted for.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of different visitation models on healthcare-associated viral gastroenteritis (HA-VGI) infection rates in a pediatric hospital. It compares HA-VGI rates across four periods with varying visitation policies, including seasonal restrictions, mandatory masking, and sibling visitation. The results show a significant decline in HA-VGI rates during Period 2 with mandatory masking, and rates in Period 3 remained lower than Period 1 despite increased sibling visitation. Community GI viral activity was independently linked to HA-VGI rates, and norovirus was predominant. The authors conclude that mandatory masking may reduce HA-VGI rates independently of seasonality and community viral activity, suggesting a potential public health strategy. However, the study's observational design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence strength is moderate.

title: Acute diarrhea following the first subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab: a case report of a probable adverse drug reaction

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report a case of acute diarrhea following the first subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab, highlighting the need for further investigation into potential adverse drug reactions associated with this PCSK9 inhibitor.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report was conducted on a 51-year-old man hospitalized for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction who received his first 600-mg subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab on 13 July 2026.
analysis.methods: The patient's symptoms were documented, and stool testing was performed to assess for pathogens, including occult blood, red blood cells, and specific viral markers, while excluding tests for rotavirus, Clostridioides difficile, norovirus, and adenovirus.
analysis.main_results: The patient developed acute diarrhea 7 h 46 min after receiving tafolecimab, characterized by 5–8 episodes daily, with loose yellow stool, positive occult blood, and red blood cells, but no white blood cells, and a negative rotavirus test. Diarrhea resolved within 2 days after treatment with fluids, montmorillonite, and loperamide hydrochloride.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The case suggests a probable adverse drug reaction to tafolecimab, as supported by the Naranjo score of 5, and highlights the importance of monitoring for new-onset diarrhea following PCSK9 inhibitor initiation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for precise temporal documentation, medication reconciliation, targeted microbiological evaluation, and pharmacovigilance reporting in cases of new-onset diarrhea after PCSK9 inhibitor use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single case report, which may not be generalizable. However, the Naranjo score of 5 provides a moderate level of confidence in the probable adverse drug reaction.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 51-year-old man who developed acute diarrhea following his first subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab, a PCSK9 inhibitor, on 13 July 2026. The patient experienced 5–8 episodes of diarrhea daily, with loose yellow stool, positive occult blood, and red blood cells, but no white blood cells or rotavirus. Diarrhea resolved within 2 days after treatment with fluids, montmorillonite, and loperamide hydrochloride. The Naranjo score of 5 indicated a probable adverse drug reaction. The case underscores the importance of monitoring for new-onset diarrhea after PCSK9 inhibitor initiation and highlights the need for targeted microbiological evaluation and pharmacovigilance reporting. While the study is limited to a single case, the findings contribute to understanding potential adverse effects of tafolecimab.

title: Yield of a multiplexed gastrointestinal polymerase chain reaction panel for evaluation of diarrhea in hospitalized patients with cancer: a diagnostic stewardship opportunity

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic yield of multiplexed gastrointestinal polymerase chain reaction (GIP) panels for detecting non-Clostridioides difficile pathogens in hospitalized cancer patients with diarrhea, addressing a gap in understanding their utility in different clinical settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study included stool tests from hospitalized adults with a cancer diagnosis from July 2021 to May 2025, focusing on patients with community versus hospital-onset diarrhea.
analysis.methods: The study used generalized estimating equations with Poisson regression to estimate the prevalence ratio of detecting ≥1 non-Clostridioides difficile targets after hospital day (HD) 3 compared to HD 1–3. The center recommends GIP primarily for patients with community-onset diarrhea and stand-alone C. difficile testing for hospital-onset diarrhea.
analysis.main_results: Among 1,433 GIPs from 1,127 patients, 468 (33%) were ordered after HD 3. difficile and norovirus were detected most frequently (16% and 6%, respectively). The prevalence ratio of detecting ≥1 non-C. difficile target after HD 3 was 0.73 (95% CI [0.53–1.00]; P = .053) compared to HD 1–3.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that the added diagnostic yield for detecting ≥1 non-C. difficile targets by GIP in patients with cancer and hospital-onset diarrhea is limited, suggesting a need to restrict GIP ordering after HD 3 on oncology units.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform diagnostic stewardship practices by highlighting the limited utility of GIPs for detecting non-C. difficile pathogens in hospitalized cancer patients with hospital-onset diarrhea, potentially reducing unnecessary testing and antimicrobial use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, which limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is based on observational data, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the diagnostic yield of multiplexed gastrointestinal polymerase chain reaction (GIP) panels for detecting non-Clostridioides difficile pathogens in hospitalized cancer patients with diarrhea. It found that GIPs were less effective in identifying such pathogens after hospital day 3 compared to earlier days, with C. difficile and norovirus being the most frequently detected. The results suggest that the added value of GIPs in this context is limited, supporting the restriction of GIP testing after HD 3 on oncology units. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on observational data result in moderate confidence in its findings, highlighting the need for further research to confirm these results and their implications for diagnostic stewardship in cancer patients with hospital-onset diarrhea.

title: Teclistamab in multiple myeloma with coexisting myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia

title: Raman-Silent-Region Encoded SERS-LFIA for Low-Background and Sensitive Multiplex Detection of Heterogeneous Food Safety Hazards

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of detecting multiple food safety hazards simultaneously in complex matrices, where traditional methods struggle with sensitivity and specificity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a multiplex SERS-LFIA platform for the detection of aflatoxin B1, norovirus genogroup I major capsid protein (NoV GI.1 VP1), and Salmonella Typhimurium in spiked real samples such as tea and soymilk.
analysis.methods: The platform utilized Raman-silent-region encoded nanoprobes, where 4-mercaptobenzonitrile was confined at the interface between the Au core and Ag shell to create a unique Raman response for each target.
analysis.main_results: The method achieved limits of detection of 3.4 pg/mL for aflatoxin B1, 12.3 pg/mL for NoV GI.1 VP1, and 1.02 × 104 CFU/mL for Salmonella Typhimurium. In spiked real samples, recoveries ranged from 85.48% to 111.95% in tea and 86.09% to 112.03% in soymilk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that the Raman-silent-region encoding and spatial discrimination across multiple test lines enable sensitive and accurate detection of chemically and biologically distinct hazards, offering a novel approach for rapid screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a new tool for the simultaneous detection of food safety hazards, which can enhance surveillance and risk assessment in public health contexts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on spiked real samples, which may not fully represent real-world complexity. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel Raman-silent-region encoded SERS-LFIA platform for the simultaneous detection of multiple food safety hazards, including norovirus genogroup I major capsid protein. The method uses nanoprobes with 4-mercaptobenzonitrile confined at the Au-Ag interface to generate unique Raman responses, minimizing interference and enabling sensitive detection. The platform was tested in spiked tea and soymilk samples, achieving recovery rates between 85.48% and 112.03% for the targets. The study highlights the potential of this approach for rapid screening in complex food matrices, though the evidence is based solely on abstract data, limiting its strength to moderate. The findings could inform improved surveillance and risk assessment for food safety.
